03 / 04 · A school team project

HANDBOOKER

Less searching. More clarity.

the idea

A student usually arrives with a question, not the name of a policy. Handbooker starts with the words they would actually use, then helps them find the relevant part of the school handbook.

Working lookup experience · renamed from Lion’s Guide
Answers,
with a source.
The project

Student experience & information design

My focus

Question flows, interface design & implementation

At a glance

Natural student wording · Source-linked answers · Clear clarification

The student’s starting point

A question,
in their own words.

Students ask about a situation: a phone in a pocket, an absence, or what they can wear. They should be able to begin there.

Handbooker connects ordinary wording, alternate phrases, and common misspellings with reviewed questions and source-backed handbook answers.

Try the actual lookup experience

Go ahead.
Ask a question.

Try “Can I keep my phone in my pocket?” or search for “dress code.” This isolated portfolio demo uses the new Handbooker name. Questions stay in your browser.

Open demo in a full window ↗
Three useful responses

Clarity includes
knowing when to ask.

A clear match leads directly to an answer and its source. A broad or ambiguous question offers options to narrow it down. A question outside the covered material receives an honest boundary.

The existing lookup uses a reviewed question bank and browser-side matching. It is a focused handbook finder, with no live AI call behind the search.

↗

A broad question

↳

Outside the handbook

See that the question is not covered, without an invented answer.

Trust in the details

An answer you can
follow back.

Source excerpts and PDF page references let the student check where an answer came from. The interface keeps that evidence close to the response.

The project was previously branded Lion’s Guide. Handbooker is its new public name; the portfolio demo adapts that branding while preserving the original lookup behavior.
